services.name: Class
services.desc: In celebration of International Underground Railroad Month this September, join Dr. John F. Leeke and his daughter, Ananda Leeke, as they share their family’s extraordinary story of freedom seekers. Through research on Ancestry.com for Dr. Leeke’s memoir, American Change Agent: A Life & Legacy of Seeking Diversity, Equality, and Inclusion, they traced their origins back to Hagerstown, Maryland, where Peter and Catherine Leek escaped to Amherstburg, Canada, alongside their 14 children. This multigenerational discussion highlights John’s early work as a pioneer for diversity, equality, and inclusion long before DEI gained widespread recognition. blurb: THE LINES WE CROSS: 250 Years of Maryland Forging America” July 31, 2026 - October 31, 2027 Maryland sits directly below the Mason-Dixon Line, a border state where freedom and slavery once existed side by side. In this landscape of impossible boundaries, Black Marylanders learned to navigate through movement, making, and profound creativity.
